target.title: fix(agents): make model-facing tool schemas llama.cpp GBNF-compatible
target.body:
Fixes #108367
Fixes #108473
Fixes #108580

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw runs against a llama.cpp `llama-server` with grammar-constrained tool calling, **every** chat request fails with a `400` as soon as grammar-hostile fields appear in the active tool list — not just cron calls. [#108580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108580) documents three distinct GBNF blockers (each masking the next):

1. **Unanchored pattern** — `declarationKey` used `pattern: "\\S"` → `Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'`.
2. **PCRE shorthand** — even anchored `^\\S+$` or `^[\\s\\S]*\\S[\\s\\S]*$` fails; llama.cpp rejects `\\S`/`\\s` unknown escapes.
3. **Oversized maxLength** — `trigger.script` `maxLength: 65536` exceeds the ~2000 GBNF repetition ceiling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Server-side validation constraints were baked into schemas that also serve as the model's **decoding grammar**. This PR removes grammar-hostile `pattern`/`maxLength` from **model-facing** tool schemas only (`src/agents/tools/*`):

| Field | Removed from model schema | Still enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| `cron` `job.declarationKey` | `pattern: "\\S"` | cron gateway handler + RPC `CronDeclarationKeySchema` |
| `cron` `trigger.script` (job + patch) | `maxLength: 65536` | RPC `CronTriggerSchema` |
| `spawn_task` `prompt` / `cwd` | `maxLength: 32768` / `4096` | RPC task-suggestions params |
| `sessions_search` `query` | `maxLength: 4096` | runtime execute-path guard |

`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` is **intentionally unchanged** (RPC contract only; never compiled into model grammar).

## User Impact

Users on llama.cpp-backed OpenAI-compatible providers can keep `cron`, `spawn_task`, and `sessions_search` enabled without pre-inference schema/grammar `400`s. Server-side validation unchanged for normal inputs.

## Evidence

### Regression guard
`src/agents/tools/tool-schema-llamacpp-compat.test.ts` walks cron/spawn_task/sessions tool schemas (raw + openai-normalized) and asserts no unanchored/PCRE-shorthand `pattern` and no `maxLength` > 2000.

### Focused tests (local, head `8bad86f1dd4`)
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/tool-schema-llamacpp-compat.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/cron-tool.schema.test.ts test/scripts/prompt-snapshots.test.ts
```
15 passed; `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` current.

### Live llama.cpp before/after proof (local)
Environment: `llama-server` b9960 (Homebrew), `ibm-granite/granite-4.1-3b-GGUF:Q4_K_M`, `--jinja`, OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/chat/completions` with the real OpenClaw cron tool schema (`normalizeToolParameterSchema`, `modelProvider: openai`).

```
llama.cpp endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1
fixed declarationKey: {"type":"string","description":"Idempotent declaration key.","minLength":1,"maxLength":200}
fixed trigger.script: {"type":"string","minLength":1,"description":"Trigger script source (max 65536 chars)."}

=== BROKEN: unanchored declarationKey pattern \\S (shipped 2026.7.1) ===
HTTP 400
error_preview: {"error":{"code":400,"message":"Unable to generate parser for this template. Automatic parser generation failed: JSON schema conversion failed:\nPattern must start with '^' and end with '$'","type":"invalid_request_error"}}

=== BROKEN: trigger.script maxLength 65536 (#108580 constraint 3) ===
HTTP 400
error_preview: {"error":{"code":400,"message":"Failed to initialize samplers: failed to parse grammar","type":"invalid_request_error"}}

=== FIXED: current PR model-facing cron schema ===
HTTP 200
inference_ok: true
reply_preview: Hello! How can I help you today?
```

**Interpretation:** shipped schema fails with the exact errors reported in #108473/#108580; this PR's model-facing schema compiles and reaches inference (HTTP 200).

### vs #108671
Same model-facing GBNF strategy as @wsyjh8's #108671. This PR adds live before/after `llama-server` proof and is rebased on current `main` with green CI (including `check-lint` after #108857 discord test split landed on main).
